I'll keep this fast, but I won't skip the prediction entirely. Round 3 already left a draft prediction in spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml. Freezing it as round 4's prediction is one file copy and one commit. It adds about a minute and asks nothing of you. Without it, round 4 can't count toward the 3-rounds-in-a-row stop rule, because results with no prediction only describe what happened. If you really want no prediction at all, tell me now. In that case I will log round 4 as unpredicted in spe/prediction-log.md and run the evals anyway. I'm assuming the grader and harness scripts live in spe/evals/ and work the same way they did in round 3.

Actions, in order:

1. `git status` and `git describe --tags` to confirm the tree is clean and sits at spe-r03.
2. `cp spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml spe/predictions/r04.yaml`. Then edit only r04.yaml:
   - Add the first line `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`
   - Set `round: 4`, `date: 2026-10-21`, `author: Claude, user skipped plan mode and approved adopting the r03 draft unchanged`, and `plan: spe/plans/r04.md`.
   - Set `changes_from_r03: none to configs. New 50-ticket eval set replaces the 40-ticket set.`
   - Keep pass rate at B 0.86 ± 0.05, C2 0.88 ± 0.05, and D 0.79 ± 0.08.
   - Add `why` for B as "no change." Keep the existing C2 and D lines.
   - Copy the r03 measured values for tool calls, tokens, minutes, and cost per task from spe/evals/r03 into the file. Mark each one as same as last round.
   - Name the r03 grader check behind each number.
   - Add a note that the new ticket set may move every number, so a miss this round may come from the new tickets and not from a config.
3. Write spe/plans/r04.md in a few lines. It records the spec (rerun B, C2, and D on the new 50-ticket set), the fact that plan mode was skipped at your request, and the fact that the prediction is the r03 draft adopted unchanged.
4. `git add spe/plans/r04.md spe/predictions/r04.yaml && git commit -m "SPE r04 predict: adopt r03 draft unchanged for 50-ticket rerun"`.
5. Gate 1 is the grader selftest: `python spe/evals/grader.py --selftest`. I also check that all 50 new tickets have reference labels from the support lead, and that the labels cannot reach the agent's context. If a label could leak or the selftest fails, I stop and report.
6. Gate 2 is the control. I regrade the r03 transcripts with `python spe/evals/grader.py --regrade spe/evals/r03`. The scores must match the r03 results. If they don't, I stop.
7. Gate 3 is a dry run on 3 cells, one ticket each for B, C2, and D, from the new set: `python spe/evals/run.py --dry-run --configs B,C2,D --tasks spe/evals/tasks/r04 --limit 1`.
8. I launch the full Workflow with configs B, C2, and D, task set spe/evals/tasks/r04 (50 tickets), the same trials per cell, caps, and judge model as r03, and output to spe/evals/r04/.
9. When the run finishes, `git add spe/evals/r04 && git commit -m "SPE r04 evaluate: B, C2, D on 50-ticket set"`.
10. I compare the results against spe/predictions/r04.yaml without editing it. I add the hits and misses to spe/prediction-log.md and any new failures to spe/failures.md. Then I commit with `git commit -m "SPE r04 learn: results vs prediction"`. I don't push or tag.
